goal: Restructure the internal C++ library layout so a slimmed-down internal kernel library only pulls in the utility code the validation engine actually needs.
Aims to complete the internal-library design in doc/design/libraries.md and make it easier to build the external libbitcoinkernel with a real dependency boundary instead of ad hoc source lists.
reviewability: Ready. CI is clean, the branch is mergeable, and the author has continuously addressed review comments across 46 force-pushes with a fresh re-ACK on 2026-09-08.
agreement: Strong support with multiple concept, approach, and code-review ACKs plus real testing (guix builds, an iPhone kernel demo app) (hebasto, ryanofsky, janb84, yuvicc, w0xlt, BrandonOdiwuor, Sjors).
ajtowns questioned whether the whole approach reduces or adds to library complexity but did not block, and the author updated the design doc in response; no standing objection remains.
Naming bikeshed (util_kernel vs kernel_util vs util_core) was never resolved definitively but is style, not a blocking concern.

result.summary: This PR introduces an internal libbitcoin_kernel static library and a slimmed-down libbitcoin_util_kernel library so the external libbitcoinkernel shared library can be built from a real, enforced internal dependency graph instead of a hand-maintained source file list. It splits src/util/CMakeLists.txt into a kernel-only subset and a full util library, updates doc/design/libraries.md and contrib/devtools/check-deps.sh accordingly, and reuses the internal libraries' source lists to build the external kernel target. A known trade-off is called out: without manual symbol export management, the change would break REDUCE_EXPORTS=ON builds, so the external library still gets a separately populated source list for now.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's build system does not currently enforce the internal library dependency boundaries described in doc/design/libraries.md, so the kernel library's actual dependencies can silently drift from what a kernel consumer needs, making it hard to know what is safe to depend on when building a minimal, embeddable libbitcoinkernel. This mainly affects kernel maintainers and downstream projects trying to build against libbitcoinkernel with minimal dependencies.

open_concerns: ajtowns thinks the overall three-plus-library split (consensus/common/util/util_kernel) is a messy way to achieve the goal and sketched an alternative topology, but did not block and the author called the impact 'pretty marginal' while remaining open to future restructuring.
achow101 and yuvicc questioned specific link dependencies (kernel link for bitcoin-cli/bitcoin-wallet, ws2_32) which were addressed by dropping the unneeded links.
Naming of the new library (util_kernel vs kernel_util vs util_core) was never fully settled.
resolved_concerns: hebasto's MSVC and CMake circular-dependency issues were fixed via subsequent pushes.
ryanofsky's concerns about file placement (bytevectorhash, readwritefile, sock, expected.cpp) were addressed by moving files back or adding them explicitly.
w0xlt's leftover readwritefile.cpp/serfloat.cpp misplacement and CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR vs PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR nits were fixed in later pushes.
Design doc omissions flagged by ajtowns (missing edges, missing libbitcoinkernel node) were added.

result.card: This PR restructures Bitcoin Core's internal CMake libraries to introduce a bitcoin_kernel and a slimmed bitcoin_util_kernel library, so the external libbitcoinkernel shared library can be built by reusing an enforced internal dependency graph instead of a manually maintained source list, per doc/design/libraries.md. It solves a build-system problem for kernel maintainers and downstream libbitcoinkernel consumers: making the kernel's real dependencies explicit and minimal ahead of exportable-symbol work. The strongest evidence of importance is years of sustained maintainer engagement (hebasto, ryanofsky, ajtowns, achow101, fanquake) and real-world validation, including a successful guix build and an external iPhone app built against the kernel with no observed behavior change. The PR is Ready to review, with CI green and mergeable, and carries Strong agreement despite an unresolved stylistic debate over whether the library topology (util/util_kernel/common/kernel) is the cleanest way to achieve the goal. It has no hard blocking dependency but is explicitly framed as groundwork for future REDUCE_EXPORTS symbol-export work and further kernel decoupling (e.g., splitting mempool policy out of the kernel).
